terms.gloss: a private tutor; fem. praeceptrīx domestica
the slave who had charge of a boy at home and took him to school; a governor, tutor
evidence: Plaut. Bacch. 138: nōn paedagōgum jam mē, sed Lȳdum vocat
Cic. Lael. 74: nūtrīcēs et paedagōgī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Greek παιδαγωγός. He looked after the boy’s conduct; the teaching was the magister’s or the praeceptor’s.

sources: Lewis & Short: praeceptor · Lewis & Short: paedagogus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 32.

phrases.latin: nōn paedagōgum jam mē, sed Lȳdum vocat
phrases.english: he no longer calls me his tutor, but plain Lydus
